sessions.title: From developers to founders: Building AI products, demos, unfiltered
sessions.description: AI lets you take an idea to a working prototype within hours. Overnight, a software developer transforms into a founder, powered by AI agents handling product development, graphic design, and operations. What does that path really look like? Learn from builders who turned into one-person companies, as they demo their real projects live on stage. No vendor bias, just honest takes on what actually works.
sessions.speakers: Hana Ahriz (Founder, Pixels & People); Daria Shevchenko (Co-founder | Customer Success Engineer, https://www.pixelsnpeople.com/)

sessions.title: Digital government, better governance: Europe's public sector transformation
sessions.description:
Featured Panelists:

Gonçalo Matias
Minister in the Cabinet of the Prime Minister and for State Reform (Portugal)

Damir Habijan
Minister of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation (Croatia)
sessions.speakers: Damir Habijan (Minister of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation, MPUDT Croatia); Gonçalo Matias (Minister in the Cabinet of the Prime Minister and of State Reform, Government of Portugal)

sessions.title: Sensing the future: Using AI to unlock the next generation of molecular science.
sessions.description: What happens when AI moves beyond digital interfaces to interact with the physical and chemical world? From digitising scent and mapping molecular behaviour to creating sustainable food systems, AI is turning raw data into real-world sensory intelligence. This session demonstrates how AI-driven science is opening up multibillion-dollar opportunities across health, consumer products and global food infrastructure.
sessions.speakers: Anshika Srivastava (COO, Apoha); Asier Alea (Director of Global Development, Basque Culinary Centre / GOe); Alex Wiltschko (CEO & Founder, Osmo); Chris Stokel-Walker (Freelance Journalist, BBC News, The New York Times, Wired)

sessions.title: The agentic internet: Who controls the web?
sessions.description: AI agents are changing how people discover information, shop, and transact online. As more activity happens without a human click, the web is facing new questions about control, attribution, and value. Cloudflare co-founder and CEO Matthew Prince explains why the internet is at a turning point - what this shift means for companies of every size and what it will take to keep the web open in the agentic era.
sessions.speakers: Matthew Prince (Co-founder & CEO, Cloudflare); Nick Thompson (CEO, The Atlantic)

sessions.title: The new geopolitics of venture capital
sessions.description: Global VC is no longer frictionless. Driven by sovereign AI mandates, trade barriers, and supply chain shifts, capital strategies are now inseparable from geopolitical ones. Join this session as we unpack how top investors are navigating cross-border friction, deploying capital, and backing the next wave of global tech leaders.
sessions.speakers: Larry Li (Founder & Managing Partner, Amino Capital); Elena Casas-Montanez (Reporter, Reuters)

sessions.title: AI’s holy grail: From uncertain systems to reliable outcomes
sessions.description: The biggest challenge in enterprise AI is execution that yields guaranteed outcomes at scale: turning rapidly evolving capabilities into systems that reliably deliver value. This session examines frameworks for engineering deterministic outcomes from inherently nondeterministic AI by bringing together highly specialized systems, frontier-level expertise and guardrails to make AI reliable at enterprise scale.
sessions.speakers: Taso Du Val (CEO, Toptal); Leandro Souza (Editor, Startups.com.br)

sessions.title: The death of marketing as we know it
sessions.description: AI agents are becoming the new gatekeepers between consumers and brands, researching products, comparing options and making decisions on our behalf. As algorithms influence what we buy, how will marketers earn attention, stand out from competitors and build lasting loyalty? Qualcomm's EVP & CMO Don McGuire discusses why the next era of marketing will demand a new approach to discovery, differentiation and trust.
sessions.speakers: Don McGuire (EVP and CMO, Qualcomm); Kit Eaton (Technology writer, INC)

sessions.title: The sovereign creator
sessions.description: Social platforms leave creators at the mercy of sudden algorithm changes and heavy revenue cuts. beehiiv Co-Founder and CEO Tyler Denk outlines the shift to direct audience ownership and shows how creators can take back control, leveraging social platforms for growth while converting followers into owned-and-operated media businesses.
sessions.speakers: Tyler Denk (Co-Founder & CEO, Beehiiv)

sessions.title: Regulation is killing European fintech
sessions.description: European regulation is simultaneously the best and worst thing about building fintech here. It protects consumers, but it also protects incumbents, raises the cost of experimentation and arguably explains a big chunk of why Europe keeps falling behind the U.S. and Asia in producing category-defining companies. In this conversation we're exploring how regulation in Europe is death by a thousand rules.
sessions.speakers: Yusuf Özdalga (Partner, QED Investors); Terry Martin (International News Anchor/Moderator, Free agent)

sessions.title: The future of enterprise software has no middleman
sessions.description: The engineering queue used to gatekeep what got built. Now, the person closest to the problem can build the solution for it: employees inside nearly two-thirds of the Fortune 500 already do. When software stops being a specialist job, that changes how companies build, staff, and ship. Anton Osika, Lovable's co-founder and CEO, will talk about what this transformation already looks like inside real companies, and what it takes to keep software secure when anyone can ship it.
sessions.speakers: Anton Osika (Co-founder & CEO, Lovable); Harry McCracken (Technology Editor, Fast Company)

Not yet in a team? Join the pre-hackathon meetup on Tuesday at 12:30pm.
